comparison: Both address the core finding about QTP uplift shifting migration patterns (C15-C20, C72). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN due to unvalidated assumptions about niche conservatism and limited tracking data, while peer reviewers rate it SUPPORTED, with the editor stating 'central claims are now solid' and praising the evidence quality.

Both evaluate the monsoon dynamics hypothesis (C21-C25, C40-C41, C73). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with minor reservations about mechanistic links, while peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED with the editor explicitly endorsing that 'monsoon dynamics, rather than elevation per se, are most consistent with observed longitudinal reorientation.'

OpenEval evaluates regional/seasonal variation in environmental drivers (C26-C33) as SUPPORTED but notes biological interpretations need mechanistic validation. Peer review R2 groups these claims with the broader monsoon findings (C21-C25, C40-C41, C73) and rates all as SUPPORTED without distinguishing regional patterns.

Both address mechanistic explanations linking monsoon dynamics to migration (C42-C50). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with note that direct empirical validation would strengthen claims. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, with the editor's endorsement of monsoon dynamics implicitly supporting these mechanistic details.

Both evaluate spring migration temperature preferences and capital breeding interpretation (C51-C55). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the breeding strategy interpretation is speculative despite statistical support. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, though with less explicit discussion than main findings.

Both address eBird data limitations and handling approaches (C56-C60). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, praising acknowledgment of limitations and best practices. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with editor noting expanded tracking data and explicit caveats strengthen the study.

OpenEval evaluates AdaSTEM methodology (C61-C63) as SUPPORTED with appropriate justification. Peer review R6 groups this with other methodological approaches (C64-C71) and rates all as SUPPORTED, praising methods as 'detailed and well-described' and 'transparent and repeatable.'

OpenEval evaluates CESM climate modeling (C64-C66) as SUPPORTED but notes unaddressed paleoclimate uncertainties. Peer review R6 groups this with broader methodological framework and rates SUPPORTED, affirming appropriateness of climate-model datasets for continent-scale analysis.

OpenEval evaluates MaxEnt methodology (C67-C70) as SUPPORTED with standard best practices. Peer review R6 includes this in overall methodological assessment rated SUPPORTED, with reviewer praising transparency and repeatability of methods.

OpenEval evaluates wind connectivity calculation (C71) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citation and clear description. Peer review R6 includes this in comprehensive methodological evaluation rated SUPPORTED without specific discussion of wind connectivity.

Both evaluate contextual background and literature framing (C1-C14, C37-C39). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and clear motivation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with reviewer praising Introduction as 'very well-written' with 'clear logical structure and good use of literature.' Peer R7 also includes C34-C36 about migration inflexibility challenges.

OpenEval evaluates claims challenging migration inflexibility views (C34-C36) as UNCERTAIN, noting the counterfactual approach infers historical patterns rather than observing behavioral flexibility. Peer review R7 groups these with broader contextual claims (C1-C14, C37-C39) and rates all as SUPPORTED, praising the logical structure without specifically addressing the inflexibility challenge.
